correctness.rationale: For every nonaxis unit x in the real smooth cubic plane, signed coordinate symmetry reduces x to (1,t)/(1+t^3)^(1/3), t>0; the unique norming functional has kernel spanned by (-t^2,1), giving precisely the ± normalized Birkhoff partner. Its reverse functional residual satisfies D(t)^3=u|1−u|^3/((1+u)(1+u^2)^2), u=t^3. Under k=|1−u|/(1+u), D^3=H(k)=k^3(1−k^2)/(1+k^2)^2, k∈[0,1]. Independent symbolic differentiation yielded H′=k^2(3−6k^2−k^4)/(1+k^2)^3; the unique interior global maximum has k^2=2√3−3, and H(k)^2=(78√3−135)/16. Endpoints (axis or t=1) give zero. For finite-dimensional real smooth strictly convex E, the duality map j_E is bijective, j_(E*)(j_E(x))=x, and (x,y)↦(j_E(y),j_E(x)) bijects the ordered Birkhoff sets while preserving |j_E(y)(x)|. Thus the dual constant and the complete orbit follow without finite sampling. The asserted duality does not include nonsmooth/non-strictly-convex spaces.
